 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Alexander Zverev will not celebrate becoming men's number one with the Vienna Open title after missing out on a spot in the final.
 The German was beaten on Saturday 4-6, 6-1, 6-7 (4-7) by Australia's Alex de Minaur, who will now face Carlos Alcaraz in title match.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Zverev repeatedly complained about the balls, which he felt bounced too high.
 "Do you think it's normal to play with these balls at a tennis tournament?" he asked the umpire.
 The German had already secured top spot in the rankings after he reached the quarter-finals in Vienna. He will take over as number one from Italy's Jannik Sinner when the rankings are updated on Monday.
 He is also guaranteed the year-end number one.
 Zverev is only the 30th tennis player to top the ATP world rankings, which were introduced in 1973.
 The last German male tennis player to hold the top spot was Boris Becker, some 35 years ago. Among German female tennis players, only Steffi Graf and Angelique Kerber have achieved this in the WTA rankings.
 This season, Zverev won his first Grand Slam at the French Open and topped that up with the US Open title.
